findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false; the feature-flag check is dead code
findings.body:
`enableSqlExpressions` reads `FlagSqlExpressions`, negates it, and then returns `false` on both branches. The flag lookup has no effect, and the function name and structure suggest the toggle still controls the feature when it does not.

This is easy to 'fix' later into `return true` while the backend is only a stub, or to misread during review. If the intent is a hard disable, replace it with an explicit constant (or remove the helper) and add a comment that SQL expressions are disabled for CVE-2024-9264 regardless of the flag.

findings.title: Existing SQL expression tests will now fail against the stub DB
findings.body:
`TablesList` now uses the stub `DB`, whose `RunCommands` always returns "not implemented". `sql.QueryFramesInto` also always errors.

Existing tests in `pkg/expr/sql` and `pkg/expr` (e.g. parser tests expecting table names, and SQL command tests calling `NewSQLCommand`/`Execute`) previously ran against DuckDB. They will now fail unless they are removed or skipped.

The PR changes no test files. Either CI breaks, or those tests should be updated to assert the disabled behaviour, for example that a SQL expression query is rejected.

findings.title: Non-reader code paths report a misleading 'error reading SQL command' instead of 'disabled'
findings.body:
`UnmarshalSQLCommand` is used by the legacy node-building path and does not go through `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`. On that path, the SQL query reaches `NewSQLCommand`, where `sql.TablesList` fails with "not implemented".

The user then gets a 400 "error reading SQL command", which suggests their SQL is malformed rather than that the feature is disabled. The 'disabled' check should be applied centrally, e.g. in `NewSQLCommand`, so every entry point returns a clear, consistent error.

findings.title: Error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' is inaccurate
findings.body:
The feature is implemented but has been deliberately disabled for security reasons. The message will confuse users who enabled the `sqlExpressions` feature flag.

A message such as "SQL expressions are disabled" would be accurate. Returning a proper `errutil` BadRequest, consistent with the other SQL errors, would also help.
